change.title: Resolve the two conditional hardware quantities
change.reason: Your diskette defaults are implemented in the two software-edition proposals, including their paired base-part definitions. The remaining quantities describe hardware, not installation media. A site survey determines network cable quantities and CP/M application qualification determines whether a hardware module is needed. The diskette default of one does not establish either hardware quantity. Please specify whether to retain these variable quantities or define a standard per-installation package.

findings.description: Network cables have a null quantity because site survey determines counts and lengths; propose a fixed package only if its scope is specified.
The CP/M-80 module is supplied only where application qualification requires it. Confirm one module per qualifying system, or retain a variable project quantity.

change.title: Define software memory and storage limits
change.reason: Provide measured or explicitly selected RAM/ROM budgets per edition and platform, distinguishing installed memory from working set and ROM occupancy.

before.title: Ecosystem growth and market response — CP/M / 8-bit era
before.description: CP/M / 8-bit ecosystem development from July 1978 through the portable-system competition milestone on 1 April 1981. Build the ecosystem of independent manufacturers, software developers and peripheral contributors around Aurelia’s CP/M with TUI, FlexiBUS, C development interfaces, graphics subsystem and digital monitor connectivity. Coordinate documented implementation and qualification, SMC second-source transfer, portable DRI extensions and Tandy cooperation. CP/M activity continues alongside the Artemis ecosystem phase; the envelope does not imply universal adoption or completion of all later targets.

participant.role: C development platform and application integration

inputs.description: Aurelia’s launch provides the working software, peripheral and display platform for independent implementations and supplier cooperation.
Use documented software APIs, bus rules, graphics profiles and monitor-link specifications, with explicit licensing and host-specific qualification.

outcomes.description: Independent contributors have a documented implementation and qualification programme covering CP/M/TUI, FlexiBUS, C development, graphics APIs and monitor connectivity. Final access terms and unverified participation remain subject to the existing agreements and qualification requirements.

The recorded milestones include portable DRI extension release, the supported Tandy configuration and initial qualified SMC chip sales. They do not establish release of every licensed chip or universal compatibility.
Microsoft BASIC has a recorded Aurelia release as independently licensed third-party software.

The closing market-response milestone records competition from bundled portable CP/M systems, making existing software libraries and total package cost important to business buyers without asserting alternative-world sales volumes or component supply.

steps.description: Transfer engineering knowledge and qualify independently manufactured SMC chips.

Document CP/M/TUI services, FlexiBUS device interfaces, the C development platform and graphics/display APIs. Provide reference integrations and conformance guidance; distinguish software API support from optional display hardware and qualified monitor connectivity.
Implement and qualify Tandy’s supported Model II CP/M, Abacus and FlexiBUS option without requiring Logix video hardware.
Begin external OEM implementations, documentation and qualification of portable CP/M extensions.
Release documented optional TUI, capability-discovery and FlexiBUS extensions for non-Logix manufacturers.
Microsoft releases licensed Microsoft BASIC for Aurelia at NCC 1979, contributing third-party language software to the ecosystem.
